(This evening through Tuesday)...
Issued at 233 PM EDT Tue Aug 11 2026

Surface analysis this afternoon continues to show a weak trough of 
low pressure stretching from northern IL across northern Indiana 
into OH. This area remains the focus for convective development. 
GOES19 shows a large thunderstorm cluster over northern Indiana, 
progressing to the southeast. Thunderstorms were found stretching 
from a LAF to Noblesville-Anderson-Muncie areas, and was sagging 
southward. Best instability across area remained southwest of the 
storms where SPC CAPE showed values over 4500 J/KG. Latest ACARS 
soundings show deep CAPE available. Aloft water vapor shows a short 
wave within the NW flow aloft over eastern IL triggering our 
convective cluster as the NW flow continue to stream from MT and WY 
to Indiana. 

This afternoon and tonight...

Convection across the northern parts of the forecast area is 
expected to continue for the next several hours as the upper wave 
continues to progress east. Thunderstorms will try to sag southward 
somewhat, where the better instability will be located. Thus will 
continue to keep high pops in place in this along and south of the 
storms through the afternoon into the evening. Additional TSRA due 
to daytime heating will be possible across southwestern central 
Indiana and lower pops will still be needed there.

HRRR shows this wave exiting by early evening, and a worked over 
atmosphere should allow storms to end leading to a mainly dry 
evening and overnight period. Some fog will be possible near LAF due 
to the high dew points remaining across the area along with the 
lingering surface boundary.  Look for overnight lows in the lower 
70s and the highest pops during the evening hours.

Wednesday...

The persistent NW flow aloft is expected to remain in place on 
Wednesday, perhaps becoming a bit more northwesterly as yet another 
short wave is expected to pass across Central Indiana within the 
flow. Again the very warm and humid air mass will be in place 
allowing for plenty of moisture and pwats once again are near values 
1.81 inches. Again ample CAPE will be in play also. Thus high pops 
will once again be used on Wednesday as this wave will pass, mainly 
in the afternoon. With a good amount of daytime heating available 
through the morning hours, high temperatures should again reach the 
upper 80s to around 90.

Wednesday Night through Thursday Night...

Through this time period there is very little change in the overall 
weather pattern. The same NW flow aloft is expected to be in place 
with several embedded waves within that flow poised to pass during 
this time period. The very warm, humid and unstable airmass will 
also remain. All of this will add up to continued chances for 
showers and thunderstorms, mainly capable of producing very heavy 
rain and damaging wings through the period. Continued pops will be 
used through the period. 

Friday through Sunday Night....

More hot and humid weather is expected through the weekend along 
with daily chances for showers and thunderstorms. Models suggest 
ridging aloft over the plains will be building across Central 
Indiana through the weekend. A few ridge riding waves within a ring 
of fire type pattern will be capable of producing occasional showers 
and storms. Further support will come from the lower levels. Here, a 
frontal boundary will be lingering across Central Indiana on Friday 
before pushing north as a warm front on Saturday ahead of low 
pressure over the plains. The low will push east of Indiana on 
Sunday, likely dragging a cold front across Central Indiana. 
Forecast soundings through Sunday show plentiful moisture available 
through the column. All of this will again necessitate pops through 
the weekend. The warm air mass will result in high temperatures in 
the upper 80s to around 90.

Monday and Tuesday...

In the wake of the front on Monday, dry air and subsidence is shown 
to arrive as high pressure from the Great Lakes builds across 
Central Indiana. Forecast soundings show a dry column and for the 
first time in what seems like a long time show zero CAPE. Aloft, 
ridging is expected to return over the Rockies resulting in NW flow 
streaming across the plains into Indiana. At the moment it appears 
that little to no forcing will be available, this we should able to 
use a dry forecast at that time given the the expected surface high 
pressure.
